The presence of a microphone is the primary difference. Almost every "gaming" headset has a microphone, and almost no audiophile grade equipment does, as such, that alone can serve as a decent litmus test (though it doesn't eliminate low quality headphones of the likes of beats and skullcandies). Gaming branded devices are seen by the audiophile community as being overpriced, and having poor sound quality, comfort, and build quality. For instance, astro a50s, seen as the top gaming headset out there, get their earcups kicked by a pair of beyerdynamic dt990s, which cost less. Even without the Dolby surround sound simulation, the wider soundstage of the beyers will help you identify position based off sound far better, and on top of that, the beyers are far superior in comfort and for listening to music.
